summary: API gateway healthcheck latency cascade leading to burst 5xx and upstream runtime crash
description: Issue summary: Customers reported a sharp increase in 5xx responses for streaming and short-text generation routes starting ~2026-03-10 01:20 UTC. Impact: multiple enterprise tenants (including Acme AI) observed failed requests and poor streaming stability for ~30 minutes with elevated error rates and degraded tail latency. Environment: prod/us-east-1; recent edge-proxy library upgrade deployed 2026-03-09 23:50 UTC.\n\nTop-level hypothesis: an interaction between the new http2/multiplexing changes in the edge proxy and the API gateway healthcheck/heartbeat path caused accept-queue and connection stall behavior. Stalled upstream detection and aggressive routing rebalancing sent bursts of traffic to a recently patched runtime model variant that has an input-length handling regression which causes gradual GPU memory growth and OOM crashes, amplifying 5xx rates.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy edge-proxy with http2 multiplexing enabled (version edge-proxy 2.14.0).
2) Send a mixed workload: 60% streaming short sessions, 40% normal completion requests at 700rps from a single region.
3) Observe API gateway healthcheck heartbeat latency increase (>200ms) for 30s and subsequent routing changes.
4) Watch for re-routed traffic hitting the model-variant tagged redwood-open-gpt-small-v2-patch2026 which shows GPU memory climb and eventually crashes the runtime pod.
observed_behavior:
- API Gateway healthcheck latencies rose from ~5ms to >200ms (spikes to 800ms).
- Connection multiplexing counters showed increased HTTP/2 stream stall metrics.
- APIGW rebalanced routes away from several upstreams; new upstream received concentrated burst.
- The patched runtime’s GPU memory usage increased steadily over ~3-7 minutes per pod until the watchdog killed the process -> 5xx and streaming disconnects.
- Error rate peak: 12% 5xx on affected routes; normal baseline <0.5%.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Aisha): Correlated spike with the edge-proxy release at 23:50 UTC. APIGW healthcheck latency rise preceded the 5xx spike by ~40s.
SRE (Liam): Confirmed accept-queue growth on apigw; connection-age distribution skewed toward older HTTP/2 streams. Edge-proxy metrics show multiplex window backpressure after upgrade.

Runtime team: Found that the model variant redwood-open-gpt-small-v2-patch2026 contains a change to tokenization preprocessor that fails to cap long-running KV cache allocations for unusually fragmented multi-part prompts; this leads to gradual GPU memory growth when a particular streaming pattern is observed.

Routing logic: APIGW healthcheck lag triggers fast-failover policy which can concentrate traffic to fewer healthy upstreams for short intervals; the rebalancing coupled with the patched runtime led to a hot-shard effect.
Hypothesis validated: replayed a repro workload in staging with same proxy version and patched runtime; reproduced rising GPU allocation and eventual runtime restart within expected timeframe.

Root cause(s): (1) edge-proxy http2 multiplexing change introduced stream stall under mixed streaming/short completion workload; (2) APIGW fast-failover/reroute crystallized the traffic into a single model-variant; (3) model-variant regression allowed unbounded growth in GPU KV/preprocess cache under those specific stream fragmentation patterns, causing OOMs and 5xx.
Related artifacts: stacktrace and core capture stored in GCS: gs://redwood-incident-dumps/2026-03-10/runtime-823-core.tar.gz, replay script: github.com/redwood/replays/issue-842314-repro
mitigation_workaround: 1) Immediate: Rolled back edge-proxy to 2.13.4 in us-east-1 at 01:38 UTC to remove the HTTP/2 multiplexing change; APIGW healthchecks returned to normal within 90s.

2) Short-term: Re-qualified the model-variant by pinning traffic away from redwood-open-gpt-small-v2-patch2026 using per-tenant routing until a patch is ready. Applied for Acme AI and other impacted tenants at 02:05 UTC.
3) Circuit breaker: Increased APIGW per-upstream connection limit and temporarily disabled the aggressive fast-failover policy to reduce hot-shard rebalancing risk.
4) Customer comms: Notified Acme AI CS lead and provided an incident summary and workaround steps; offered dedicated verification window.
5) Monitoring: Added a new alert on per-upstream GPU memory gradient > 1GB/2min to detect similar regressions early.
resolution_notes: Fix implemented: Runtime team merged a patch that bounds the preprocess/KV cache allocation and adds defensive GC triggers for streaming fragmentation (PR #4287). Patch landed 2026-03-11 16:12 UTC.
Edge-proxy: Rework of HTTP/2 multiplexing was deferred; new version 2.14.1 (with backpressure fixes) will be staged after additional load testing.

Deployment plan: Patched runtime rolled out to canary in us-east-1 on 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC and to all active clusters by 2026-03-11 23:15 UTC. Watched for GPU memory gradient and 5xx; error rates returned to baseline within 7 minutes post-rollout.

Post-incident actions: Confluence postmortem created (see link below). Recommended changes: improve APIGW failover smoothing, add pre-release performance test for new edge-proxy http2 settings, enforce KV/preprocess memory caps at model-variant onboarding.
Status: Resolved for customer-facing impact; ongoing follow-up for platform hardening and improved pre-release test coverage.
